# Course Description

This course serves as a continuation of **STT 3851 (Statistical Learning I)**. Fundamentals of Generalized Linear Models (GLMs) are explored, with a focus on the linear exponential family, link functions, and their applications to categorical and count response variables.

Supervised learning techniques for classification models and tree-based methods are also examined as they apply to both regression and classification problems. Unsupervised learning is introduced, including principal component analysis and various clustering algorithms.

Other topics, such as support vector machines, regression splines, and smoothing splines, may be included. Students will complete projects using methods and algorithms covered in class and report their results using professional editing tools and principles of reproducible statistical research.

# Learning Outcomes

At the completion of this course, students will be able to:

<div class="outcome-box">

- Understand key concepts of statistical learning and the R programming language.
- Explain models in R and access and interpret output, including diagnostics.
- Understand key concepts concerning the construction of generalized linear models.
- Apply key concepts concerning principal component analysis.
- Apply key concepts concerning decision tree models.
- Apply key concepts concerning cluster analysis.
- Write professional reports and clearly explain findings related to statistical models and code.

</div>

# Assessments

<div class="assessment-box">

### Homework
Students are expected to work all assigned problems. Only selected assignments or portions of assignments may be graded. See the **Course Schedule** for due dates.

</div>

<div class="assessment-box">

### Quizzes
Weekly quizzes are anticipated throughout the semester. See the **Course Schedule** for quiz dates.

</div>

<div class="exam-box">

### Midterm Exam & Project
One **midterm exam** and one **project** will be given during the semester. See the **Course Schedule** for dates and deadlines.

</div>

<div class="exam-box">

### Final Exam
A comprehensive final exam will be given on **TBA** and will cover all material presented during the course.

As the final exam needs to be proctored, students are required to have their video camera on during the final exam period.

</div>
